results.title: TwoBucket vs Square Appointments · TwoBucket
results.content:
Booking first, quote later. Square Invoices is included on every plan, and Square can send estimates and invoices. But we didn’t find a Square page that describes an online booking turning into an estimate. On TwoBucket, the quote and invoice editor starts from the customer’s request with the services already priced.

Square’s plans are written for any appointment business. Square describes Free as “for solo professionals,” Plus as “for growing teams,” and Premium as “for large salons with complex staff management and booking needs.” Nothing in those descriptions is about vehicles or driving to a customer.

App updates. Seven reviews between July 23 and October 19, 2026 complained about updates. Each is one person’s report, and almost none of the reviews we read were from detailers. [...] Nothing we could find is built around a vehicle. We found no place in Square’s booking flow for vehicle make, model, size or condition. On Plus, Premium, or Free with advanced bookings, you can add up to 5 custom questions, but Square’s help page says those fields are optional for clients. A detailer needs to know whether the SUV has dog hair or mold before driving out.

Free stops short of protecting a day of driving. Cancellation policies, no-show fees and full prepayment are gated to Plus at $49/month, and Google Calendar sync is on Plus and Premium (Square’s help article doesn’t list Free). Deposits on Free apply only to bookings customers make online. Free also charges 3.3% + 30¢ per online card payment, against 2.9% + 30¢ on Plus. [...] ### 3. A small team that listens and moves fast

TwoBucket is new, founded in 2026. That means when you email, you reach the people who build it, and they reply within 1 business day.

If something you need is missing, you can tell us. Square has a long track record (4.88 stars from 195,326 ratings on the US App Store as of November 2026), but phone support on Free covers only the first 90 days.
